title: PRD: Proactive Quality-Gated Slimline Hosted Endpoint Suite (Chat + Embeddings + Rerank)
creator: Priya Kapoor
description: Summary: Deliver a minimal hosted endpoint bundle that exposes chat (one-shot and streaming), embeddings, and a rerank endpoint optimized for low operational complexity and gated by automated quality checks. The goal is a fast-to-ship, production-safe surface for customers who want predictable behavior and transparent degradation modes. This PRD captures requirements, behavioral contracts, acceptance criteria, and a launch checklist with staged rollout gates.
goals: 1) Ship a cohesive, minimal API surface for Chat, Embeddings, and Rerank that developers can adopt in 30 minutes with sample code. 2) Ensure deterministic degradation behavior with measurable quality gates (latency, correctness, token cost). 3) Provide an automated launch checklist and telemetry gating to stop rollout when regressions exceed thresholds.
non_goals: 1) Full-feature parity with Dedicated or Private lanes (no per-tenant on-prem packaging). 2) Advanced model composition or multi-model orchestration at launch. 3) Enterprise billing integrations or complex tenancy migration tooling.
user_personas:
- Developer (PLG): wants a small surface to prototype quickly and clear cost/latency expectations.
- Product engineer (SMB): needs predictable fallbacks and simple SDK samples.
- Platform operator (enterprise): expects telemetry and canary rollback hooks (limited in this slimline release).
api_surface: Chat endpoint: /v1/chat.generate -> supports streaming and non-streaming; request arguments: messages, max_tokens, temperature, top_p, stop, functions (optional). Embeddings endpoint: /v1/embeddings.create -> single and batched inputs; deterministic hashing of inputs for caching. Rerank endpoint: /v1/rerank.score -> candidate list + query payload, returns normalized scores and top-K ordering with stable tie-breaking.
behavioral_contracts:
- Determinism: non-streaming chat with fixed seed and temperature=0 should be stable across a bound of minor runtime patches.
- Latency SLO: p95 <= 400ms for embeddings (single), p95 <= 1200ms for chat (non-streaming), p95 <= 800ms for rerank (top-10).
- Graceful fallback: if primary model is unavailable, route to a compatible, lower-cost variant with a header: X-Redwood-Fallback.
- Cost transparency: token usage returned in response metadata for each request.
- Partial failures: In rerank, when a candidate batch partially fails, return scores for succeeded items and an errors array referencing original indices.
requirements: Functional: 1) SDKs updated (Python/Node) with examples. 2) OpenAPI schema and behavioral tests. 3) Canary automation to ramp traffic and evaluate signals. Non-functional: 1) Telemetry hooks for latency, top-k accuracy (rerank), embedding cosine distribution shifts, token-cost breakdown. 2) Ops runbook for rollback and cutover. 3) Documentation (quickstart + migration notes).
scope_changes:
- Initial scope included tenant-specific emergency quotas and fine-grained tenant billing signals. Removed from launch to reduce complexity and meet schedule.
- Added deterministic tie-breaker for rerank after early QA flagged nondeterministic ordering for identical scores.
- Reduced initial regional footprint to us-east-1 + eu-west-1 (APAC deferred).
acceptance_criteria:
1) Behavioral tests: chat, embedding, rerank suites pass against golden prompt sets (>= 98% pass rate on smoke evals).
2) Telemetry: baseline latency/throughput set; canary shows no >10% regression on p95 latency and no >2% regression on rerank top-1 accuracy across 24-hour canary at 5% traffic.
3) SDKs: examples in Python and Node validated by CI samples.
4) Rollback automation: one-click rollback reduces traffic to previous stable variant within 5 minutes.
5) Documentation: Quickstart guides completed and reviewed by DX team.
6) Security: threat model review complete (no high-severity findings).
7) Observability: cost-per-token and token breakdown available in Console for sample tenant and for canary traffic.
8) Ops runbook: incident playbook with escalation contacts and postmortem template published.
launch_checklist: 1) Pre-launch: create feature flag and default off. 2) Run full smoke evals on staging with golden prompt corpus. 3) Validate SDK release candidates and publish docs. 4) Configure canary auto-ramp: 0% -> 5% (24h) -> 25% (24h) -> 100% (48h) with gating script. 5) Canary gating: stop and rollback if p95 latency regression >10% or rerank top-1 drop >2% or embedding drift beyond threshold. 6) Run manual exploratory QA on streaming behavior. 7) Verify fallback headers and logging. 8) Confirm billing metering for token breakdown ingested by billing pipeline. 9) Run chaos test: simulated model eviction and verify graceful fallback. 10) Post-launch: monitor first-week telemetry daily and produce a 7-day launch report.
rollout_plan:
Phase 0: Staging verification (internal only) - run 100% synthetic traffic and golden suite.
Phase 1: Canary (5%) - 24h, automated quality gates; collect telemetry.
Phase 2: Expanded Canary (25%) - 24h, include small set of beta customers.
Phase 3: Full Launch (100%) - 48h monitored; rapid rollback enabled.
Post Launch: 7-day monitoring with daily sync between PM, Eng, DX, and Support.
decisions_and_tradeoffs:
- Tradeoff: shipping a slimline bundle reduces feature scope but accelerates time-to-market and reduces operational burden.
- Decision: limit regional footprint at launch to decrease cross-region deployment complexity.
- Decision: deterministic rerank tie-breaker introduced, sacrificing minimal randomness in tie scenarios to improve reproducibility for customers.
risks_and_mitigations:
Risk: quality regressions from runtime kernel updates. Mitigation: pin serving kernel version for canary and require runtime-compat tests before broad ramp.
Risk: customer confusion about fallback variants. Mitigation: include clear header and documentation, and sample code for checking X-Redwood-Fallback.
Risk: hidden token cost spikes due to streaming behavior. Mitigation: token breakdown in responses and post-call telemetry alerts for anomalous cost change.
open_questions:
1) Should we include per-request deterministic seed option in the initial API? (tradeoff: surface complexity vs reproducibility)
2) Do we need an explicit 'strict' rerank mode that fails on partial candidate errors?
3) What SLA tiers will be offered for this slimline lane at GA?

notes:
- This PRD intentionally targets a minimum viable operational footprint while preserving behavioral guarantees.
- After GA, plan a Phase 2 with APAC expansion and tenant billing signals.
- Keep an explicit migration note for Dedicated customers who may rely on advanced routing and per-tenant quotas.
